title: An ordinary week, reviewed
hook: Yan Hui, one dish of rice in a narrow lane, and a joy hardship couldn't change
tomorrow: why would a teacher point at sheep eating grass?

segments.voice: The spice box went around: rest arrives on time, and you may regard the work as done. Now the week is over. Time to look back at it.
screen: `REST ARRIVES ON TIME.` → `NOW, LOOK BACK AT THE WEEK.`

segments.voice: Scroll back through this week's photos: a parking lot, a bowl of noodles, a receipt you meant to keep. Nothing you'd post. Seven plain days, gone. Confucius had a student named Yan Hui who lived on less than that. The Analects, the collected sayings of Confucius, picture him with a single bamboo dish of rice, a single gourd of water, living in a narrow little lane. Others, Confucius says, couldn't have stood it. And then comes the surprising part.
screen: `SEVEN PLAIN DAYS, GONE.` → `ONE DISH OF RICE. ONE GOURD.` → `A NARROW LANE.`

segments.voice: He says the hardship never changed Hui's joy. Admirable, he calls him, and says it twice. Of himself, in another saying, Confucius says the same: with coarse rice to eat, water to drink, and a bent arm for a pillow, there is still joy in it. Notice what they aren't saying. They aren't saying poverty is good, or that wanting less will make you feel more. Confucius is honest that the lane was hard. The joy wasn't in the rice. It was in the Way, the life of learning and goodness they were walking, and plain days couldn't reach it. Later Confucian teachers turned this into a question for their students: find where Confucius and Yan Hui found their joy. That's the Confucian picture of joy: it lives in how you live, and and it changes how a week looks from Sunday night. A plain week isn't an empty one. If you were honest, kind and paying attention, through the parking lot and the noodles, it was plain and good.
screen: `HARDSHIP DIDN'T CHANGE HIS JOY.` · `A BENT ARM FOR A PILLOW.` · `THE JOY IS IN THE WAY.` · `FIND WHERE THEIR JOY WAS.` · then, large: `PLAIN AND GOOD.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and something to write on. Look back over the last seven days and write one plain line that was also good, like: Tuesday, soup with a friend. Read it once, then sit with it until the bell.
An ordinary week: seven plain days, looked back on the way Confucius looked at Yan Hui's narrow lane.
Your line: plain and good. Yan Hui's joy never lived in the rice. That's the week, done.

screen: `DAY 1769 COUNTS.` → `ORDINARY DAYS · 14 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: WHY WOULD A TEACHER POINT AT SHEEP EATING GRASS?`

howItsDone: Readers of the Analects return to Yan Hui's narrow lane as a picture of joy in the Way; people who borrow it look back over a plain week and write down what was good in how they lived it.

myth: Confucius taught that being poor is good in itself
the popular misreading. he says others couldn't endure that lane; the joy was in the Way, not the poverty.
Confucius praised Yan Hui because hardship didn't change his joy
he calls Hui admirable, twice, in the same saying.

fork.setup: your brother calls his week 'nothing': work, gym, frozen dinners. he was honest and kind the whole way through. what fits the Confucian teaching?
options: plain and good: the joy is in how he lived, not in what happened.
a lost week: joy needs something special to happen in it.
it's only good if he cuts back to the bare minimum, like Hui did.
fork.reveal: Yan Hui's joy wasn't in the rice or the lane. it was in the Way he walked, which a plain week can't take away.

original.note: Chinese, from the Analects: he did not change his joy, said of Yan Hui in his narrow lane.

trapdoor: what you thought: a good week needs a highlight.
what it means: for Confucius, joy can live in how you walk the Way, so plain days stay good.
what a scholar hears: Analects book six (the dish and the gourd) and book seven (the bent arm); later Confucian teachers asked students to find where Confucius and Yan Hui found their joy.
guess: seven plain days, looked back on as still good
a week with nothing done and nothing to show
the five working days, not counting the weekend

chat.says: Inés asked how my first week with Lucía went. i said 'fine.' was the whole week kind of nothing?
options: plain isn't empty: like Yan Hui's narrow lane, the joy is in how you lived it.
kind of, yes; a week only counts when something memorable happens.
it'll matter later, once you can point to what all of it led to.
chat.meaning: Yan Hui lived on one dish of rice in a narrow lane, and Confucius praised him: hardship never changed his joy. Plain can be good.

the Way.meaning: in Confucian teaching, the path of learning and goodness
